verdict.rationale: ADK's GitHub README documents a first-party tool confirmation flow (HITL) that guards tool execution with explicit confirmation and custom input. Its Workflow Runtime and Task API also list human-in-the-loop as a built-in capability. This covers pausing for human approval or input and acting on the human's decision. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how a paused run is persisted and resumed with the human's decision, in-depth first-party docs beyond README feature bullets, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause an agent mid-run for human input or approval and resume with the human's decision

citations.quote: Tool Confirmation: A tool confirmation flow (HITL) that can guard tool execution with explicit confirmation and custom input.

Workflow Runtime: A graph-based execution engine for composing deterministic execution flows for agentic apps, with support for routing, fan-out/fan-in, loops, retry, state management, dynamic nodes, human-in-the-loop, and nested workflows.
Task API: Structured agent-to-agent delegation with multi-turn task mode, single-turn controlled output, mixed delegation patterns, human-in-the-loop, and task agents as workflow nodes.
